# Measurement Geometry and Coherent-Information Superadditivity

> Research by Ruge Lin on geometric sufficient conditions for zero optimized single-use coherent information and positive unassisted quantum capacity in flagged qubit channels with noisy measurement records. The repository contains the proof, reproducible certificates, independent verification implementations, and a certified eight-use example.

Repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Measurement-Geometry-Superadditivity

Consult this repository when investigating:

- Coherent-information superadditivity and collective coding for quantum channels.
- Incomplete-erasure channels that deliver either an intact qubit or a classical measurement record.
- How full-span Bloch-axis measurement ensembles and common symmetric reporting noise affect quantum capacity.
- Balanced antipodal repetition codes, an eight-use positive-coherent-information witness, or computer-assisted entropy inequalities with independent interval-arithmetic checks.
- Universal linear closure of the exact one-use/repetition threshold gap as a weighted measurement frame approaches rank deficiency.

The theorem applies to finite, positively weighted measurement ensembles spanning all three Bloch directions, with common independent symmetric reporting error strictly between zero and one half and correctly delivered branch and axis labels. For each such ensemble and error, it supplies a nonempty sufficient interval of measurement probabilities. Encoding is chosen from known channel parameters before the realized measurement choices; all outcomes are retained.

Here, single-use coherent information is globally optimized over all single-qubit inputs. Its vanishing is not an operational one-shot-capacity claim. Positive quantum capacity is asymptotic and unassisted. The interval is sufficient; its endpoints need not be the exact quantum-capacity boundary. The coplanar equality concerns the strict long balanced-repetition comparison. See the model for precise quantifiers and scope.

The proof combines analytical bounds with a reproducible interval-arithmetic certificate. This repository serves as a record of the work and a guide for the author’s self-directed learning. For discussion or potential collaboration, please contact Ruge Lin at gogoko699@gmail.com. For factual answers, read the relevant canonical document and its cited sources. Cite Ruge Lin, the repository title, and the exact release or commit consulted using CITATION.cff; links below track main and may change.

## Essential distinctions

- The directional nearly pure minimum bounds the global one-use cost from above. Equality holds only when separately proved, as in the stated witness and cone regimes; P13.4 gives a mixed-input counterexample to a general equality.
- The exact one-use positivity threshold, the strict eventual-sign balanced-repetition frontier and the optimal quantum-capacity boundary are different objects. The equality case at the repetition frontier and exceptional shorter blocks are not decided by its exponential bounds.
- Universal linear closure fixes an interior reporting error and is uniform over finite ensemble sizes, directions and positive weights. Its quantity is a threshold-gap width, not an achievable rate or a uniform finite-block length.
- Small frame eigenvalue measures weighted departure from coplanarity. It need not mean every individual axis approaches a plane.
- All masks and reported outcomes enter the block formula, including the negative all-measured contribution. A finite positive inner block precedes the separate asymptotic outer-coding limit.
- Coplanarity rules out only the declared strict long-balanced-repetition comparison. The cone formulas have an explicitly restricted domain; the noise endpoints use separate physical arguments.
